UPSTREAM: platform/x86: intel_pmc_core: Show Latency Tolerance info This adds support to show the Latency Tolerance Reporting for the IPs on the PCH as reported by the PMC. The format shown here is raw LTR data payload that can further be decoded as per the PCI specification. This also fixes some minor alignment issues in the header file by removing spaces and converting to tabs at some places. wilco_ec: Enable WILCO_EC kernel configs if enabled by USE flag To build kernel support for the Wilco Embedded Controller, we need some kernel configs set. However, we can't add them to the common .configs within the kernel, since doing so would break some other chromebooks. We need the configs set just for Wilco. Specifically, CONFIG_WILCO_EC depends upon CONFIG_CROS_EC_LPC_MEC, but we can't enable CONFIG_CROS_EC_LPC_MEC for all boards, since that would break all boards that don't use the Microchip EC. So for only Wilco we need to enable CONFIG_CROS_EC_LPC_MEC and all the desired CONFIG_WILCO_* configs. A solution to this has already been similarly implemented for other boards, so that each board gets a custom config. Specifically, in src/overlays/baseboard-glados/profiles/base/make.defaults the cros_ec_mec USE flag is set. Then, in src/third_party/chromiumos-overlay/eclass/cros-kernel2.eclass, some kernel configs are modified when that use flag is set. This commit sets the kernel configs when the proper USE flag is set. At this point the configs are set to compile as modules. This is for development, in production we want to change the "m"s to "y"s BUG=b:124470322 TEST=manual: After applying CL:1474707 as well, the kernel builds with the wilco modules CQ-DEPEND=CL:1474707 Change-Id: I5e9eb13cd7a6dc9cb03ecad1aaff45f51e1859ef Signed-off-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1474254 Reviewed-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-by: Chris McDonald <cjmcdonald@chromium.org>

sarien: Add wilco_ec USE flag for custom kernel config To build kernel support for the Wilco Embedded Controller, we need some kernel configs set. However, we can't add them to the common .configs within the kernel, since doing so would break some other chromebooks. We need the configs set just for Wilco. Specifically, CONFIG_WILCO_EC depends upon CONFIG_CROS_EC_LPC_MEC, but we can't enable CONFIG_CROS_EC_LPC_MEC for all boards, since that would break all boards that don't use the Microchip EC. So for only Wilco we need to enable CONFIG_CROS_EC_LPC_MEC and all the desired CONFIG_WILCO_* configs. A solution to this has already been similarly implemented for other boards, so that each board gets a custom config. Specifically, in src/overlays/baseboard-glados/profiles/base/make.defaults the cros_ec_mec USE flag is set. Then, in src/third_party/chromiumos-overlay/eclass/cros-kernel2.eclass, some kernel configs are modified when that use flag is set. This commit enables the wilco_ec USE flag, that will get picked up by the eclass, which will turn on the proper kernel configs. Revert "shill: Distinguish between an unknown failure and no failure at all" This reverts commit a50ebd09191520f708ada737ef24223e9552541a. Reason for revert: Chrome needed some updates to not make this break connections. We are simply waiting for the below CL to go into a Chrome version that cros builds with; reverting until then. https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/1470746 Original change's description: > shill: Distinguish between an unknown failure and no failure at all > > Prior to this CL, kFailureUnknown was used to represent both an unknown > failure and for no failure. This is incovenient for a number of reasons, > and led to logs indicating unknown failure when completely normal > control flow occurs. > > This change adds kFailureNone to be used as the value representing no > failure. kFailureUnknown is moved to a different value such that > kFailureNone may be value 0. While this affects existing metrics, the > metrics we have on kFailureUnknown are mostly useless, as we cannot > distinguish between real failures and no failures anyways. > > Note that for cellular, any disconnects from PPP still result in setting > the failure to kFailureUnknown, even if the disconnect is not the result > of any failure. Changing this behavior requires either modifying how shill > interacts with pppd through the PPP class or assuming that a PPP > disconnect after successful authentication is intentional. > > A very similar CL was originally written by @semenzato many moons ago: > https://android-review.googlesource.com/c/platform/system/connectivity/shill/+/209433 > > BUG=chromium:596197 > TEST=- Normal state changes in shill are now logged without indicating an > unknown failure, while state changes due to actual failures do show > a failure. > - All unit tests are passing. > > Change-Id: I76970f613ec997a6dbedf6edfaead31592ada455 > Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1452314 > Commit-Ready: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> > Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> > Reviewed-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@chromium.org> > Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org> Bug: chromium:596197 Change-Id: I3775f2d260e3c223171945d774a266bda161f481 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1474562 Commit-Ready: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org>
